# Lane 06 r6 — M4 Calibrate: the evidence, generated by a script, and the README (last item)

**Workspace:** `tsr-engine` on branch `lane/calibrate` (tip `bc67eb4` or later).
**Owns:** `scripts/m4-evidence.sh` (new), `docs/m4-evidence.md`, `crates/tsr-learn/README.md`.
**Never edits:** any code, test or fixture (`crates/**/src`, `crates/**/tests`, `fixtures/`), `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, the repository `README.md`, lane 01's files, anything lanes 04 or 05 own. If the script exposes a defect, do not fix it: stop and report it to the operator.
**Reads first:** `AGENTS.md`; this file; `specs/lanes/06-calibrate.md` (the original brief — its acceptance commands and Definition of done); `specs/lanes/06rr-calibrate-repair2.md` item (8) (what the evidence must hold); `specs/lanes/reviews/m4-r5b6-review.md` (lows 3–6) and `specs/lanes/reviews/m4-r5b7-review.md`, otherwise the "known limitations" listed below; the current `docs/m4-evidence.md` and `crates/tsr-learn/README.md`; then only the files named here.

## Goal

One item: docs/m4-evidence.md has been hand-captured and has gone stale with every repair. Replace hand capture with a script, then make the README match the code. (a) Write scripts/m4-evidence.sh: run from the workspace root with `bash scripts/m4-evidence.sh > out.md`, no network, exit 0; it builds the binary, works only in a fresh directory under target/ (never in fixtures/ or the tree), and for every claim the doc makes prints the exact command (prefixed `$ `) followed by its real stdout, stderr and exit code in a fenced block: every acceptance command of the original brief on the synthetic corpus (dataset --by time --calibrate 0.2 --holdout 0.2 --seed 7, fit, verify, verify --rebuild, report, report --json, apply); `dataset --by repo` and its fit; `apply` on a task; `verify` on a copy of the bundle with a tampered manifest field and on a copy with `code_commit` edited (print what the binary does — the doc must describe that output exactly as printed and must not claim a refusal the binary does not make); `report` on a foreign dataset; then `rustc --version`, `git rev-parse HEAD`, fmt, clippy and the full `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` summary (every `test result:` line and the name of every failed test, parsed from the `---- <name> stdout ----` and `test <name> ... FAILED` lines). The base for any diff it prints is `$TSR_MAIN` if set, else `git merge-base HEAD origin/main`. (b) Generate docs/m4-evidence.md by running the script on the final tip and pasting its output unchanged; prose between blocks stays only where it is true: the first paragraph names the script and the commit it ran at; the headline comparison is stated exactly as `report` prints it (Brier and log loss for both forecasters on the same rows, the per-task paired difference with its interval, overall and per family) followed by one plain sentence saying whether the controller beats the generator on this synthetic corpus; a "Known limitations" section lists, as current behaviour: an `--out` directory the user cannot write to, and `fit`/`apply` on an unwritable dataset, still exit 1; `fit` with `holdout-access.jsonl` as a directory exits 1; `report` with `<bundle>.report.json` or `.txt` as a directory exits 1 after printing; the `--out` create probe leaves empty ancestor directories behind when a later step refuses; `dataset --store` reads the whole file to check its header and a store with a valid header but a corrupt body exits 1; the default store path creates an empty store when none exists; `counts_digest` sits outside the bundle id (a consistent edit of a count and its digest is accepted); the synthetic corpus is not real sessions. (c) crates/tsr-learn/README.md: every command and flag matches `tsr train --help` and each subcommand's `--help` on the tip; an "Apply" section shows `tsr train apply` with its real output (raw p, p with the calibrator version or `uncalibrated`, support); the input rules (what is refused, with exit 2 naming the file and field) are summarised in a few lines; no claim the evidence doc does not show. Re-running the script on the same commit reproduces every block except test timings and timestamp-derived ids, which the doc names. Conventional commit(s): one for the script, one for the generated doc and README. Operator notes: this run has ONE item; do it with one implementation task and one review task, nothing else. A create_task refused three times with the same text is a signal, not a retry — stop, post the refusal to the operator, and wait. A passing command is recorded once; do not run a green test again to confirm it. await_task waits at least 60 seconds. Start every command with `export PATH=/usr/local/cargo/bin:$PATH CARGO_HOME=$PWD/.cargo-home` (rust 1.90 with rustfmt and clippy); .cargo-home/ and target/ are build caches — never commit them, exclude them from grep and surveys. Scratch files go under target/ or a temp dir, never in the tree, and never `git add` them. If a cargo command reports "can't find crate", run it once in CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$PWD/target-fresh instead of repeating it. After every edit_file, check with grep or git diff in run_command before building; if the shell still shows the old bytes, write the file once from run_command and move on. A command that waits on the build lock is not to be re-issued: its result will arrive as a message. Commit as soon as the test passes. The run is not finished until the director itself has run `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` on the final tip; the two Docker-only m0 tests fail where Docker is absent and are not yours. Every file write goes through the sandbox, never a host path. A review verdict names the file, the line and the behaviour it saw, and says which tests it ran and which were skipped or ignored. No reply needed.

## Definition of done

scripts/m4-evidence.sh exists, runs from the workspace root with no network, and exits 0. Running it on the final tip and diffing its output against docs/m4-evidence.md's command blocks shows no difference except test timings and the named timestamp-derived ids. The doc names the script and the commit, states the headline exactly as `report` prints it with a plain sentence on the verdict, describes the code_commit edit as the binary actually handles it, and lists the known limitations above. crates/tsr-learn/README.md's commands match `--help` and include an Apply section. No code, test or fixture changed. cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast passes on the final tip apart from the two m0 tests that fail where a docker CLI answers without a daemon.

## Out of scope

Any code change (report defects to the operator instead); the repository README.md (updated when the lane lands); the real exit evidence on M3's corpus.
